S16v8ev-H1:
AI-Generated (170 words): Practice Comes Before Property
Most people building community do it in the wrong order. Get the land first! Put the vision in a document! Let whoever had the money end up owning it! And the emotional preparation? That can wait until later, when everyone has more time.
The better order is less cinematic, more like this: practice together, process a real conflict, clarify your values, test membership, decide ownership and exit, and only then think about land. I know, it wouldn't make much of a movie!
And the money side should go in stages too: don't try to fly straight to the economic destination! Only once the group can reliably provide for everybody, and fairly decide who gets what from the common, should it move to a common purse. And cutting back on outside money, or getting rid of it? That should come from what the group has shown it can do. Not from deciding that "money is impure!" while somebody else is quietly paying the tax bill.
